bull.b: TTM free cash flow of roughly $2.8B, strong year-over-year growth, and conversion near 81% of net income indicate that reported profitability is translating into cash. This gives DoorDash internal funding for product, logistics, and market expansion while improving financial resilience.

The shift from sizable losses to positive earnings across 2024–2026 represents a meaningful improvement in the business model. Steady-to-improving gross margin also supports operating leverage, suggesting DoorDash can convert continued scale and efficiency gains into stronger earnings over time.

Expansion beyond restaurants into grocery and other categories broadens DoorDash’s addressable demand and increases opportunities for higher order frequency. Rising basket sizes, frequency, and non-restaurant MAUs, combined with expected gross-profit positivity, support a more diversified and durable platform.

bear.b: Revenue growth has moderated substantially from earlier years, while operating and net margins remain modest despite DoorDash’s scale. This leaves less room for execution mistakes and means future earnings expansion will depend on sustaining efficiency improvements rather than relying solely on marketplace growth.

Although current leverage is described as manageable, the increase from historically very low debt-to-equity levels reduces some financial flexibility. Higher leverage can make DoorDash more sensitive to margin compression or slower growth and may constrain capital allocation if operating conditions weaken.

DoorDash is pursuing several large initiatives simultaneously, including autonomy, fulfillment infrastructure, merchant services, and a unified technology stack. These programs may strengthen the platform, but their complexity increases execution and timing risk and could delay expected benefits or pressure operating performance.
